en: And Nasr ibn 'Ali al-Jahdami narrated to us: Abu Ahmad narrated to us: Sufyan narrated to us, from Abu Hayyan, from Abu Zur'ah, who said: They discussed the Hour in the presence of Marwan, so 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) saying... the like of the hadith of both of them, and he did not mention 'in the forenoon'.

And Muhammad ibn 'Abdullah ibn Numayr narrated to us: my father narrated to us: Abu Hayyan narrated to us, from Abu Zur'ah, who said: Three persons among the Muslims sat with Marwan ibn al-Hakam in Medina and heard him narrating about the signs, that the first of them to emerge would be the Dajjal. Thereupon 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr said: 'Marwan said nothing; I memorized a hadith from the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) which I have not forgotten since: I heard the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) saying...' and he mentioned the like of it.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Bishr narrated to us, from Abu Hayyan, from Abu Zur'ah, from 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr, who said: I memorized a hadith from the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) which I have not forgotten since: I heard the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) saying: 'Indeed, the first of the signs to appear is the rising of the sun from its place of setting, and the emergence of the beast to the people in the forenoon; and whichever of the two comes before its companion, the other is right upon its heels shortly thereafter.'

Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to me: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us, from an-Nu'man ibn Salim, who said: I heard Ya'qub ibn 'Asim ibn 'Urwah ibn Mas'ud say: I heard a man say to 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr, 'You say that the Hour will occur at such-and-such time.' So he said, 'I was on the verge of not narrating anything to you at all! I only said that you would see a momentous matter shortly'—and that was the burning of the House, Shu'bah said this or something similar. 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'The Dajjal will emerge among my Ummah...' and he conveyed the hadith like the hadith of Mu'adh, and he said in his hadith: '...so that there will not remain anyone in whose heart is the weight of an atom of faith except that it will take him.' Muhammad ibn Ja'far said: Shu'bah narrated this hadith to me several times, and I recited it back to him.

'Ubaydullah ibn Mu'adh al-'Anbari narrated to us: my father narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us, from an-Nu'man ibn Salim, who said: I heard Ya'qub ibn 'Asim ibn 'Urwah ibn Mas'ud ath-Thaqafi say: I heard 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr—when a man came to him and said: 'What is this hadith that you narrate, saying that the Hour will occur at such-and-such time?' So he said: 'Glory be to Allah'—or 'There is no god but Allah', or a phrase like them—'I was on the verge of never narrating anything to anyone ever again! I only said that you would soon see a momentous matter: the House will be burned, and such and such will happen.' Then he said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'The Dajjal will emerge among my Ummah and will remain for 40—I do not know whether 40 days, 40 months, or 40 years—then Allah will send 'Isa ibn Maryam, looking as though he were 'Urwah ibn Mas'ud, and he will pursue him and destroy him. Then the people will remain for 7 years with no enmity between any two individuals. Then Allah will send a cool wind from the direction of ash-Sham, and there will not remain upon the face of the earth anyone in whose heart is the weight of an atom of good or faith except that it will take his soul, even if one of you were to enter the innermost part of a mountain, it would enter upon him until it takes him.' He said: I heard it from the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace). He said: 'Then there will remain the worst of people, having the lightness of birds and the minds of beasts; they will neither recognize good nor denounce evil. Then Satan will appear to them in human form and say, "Will you not respond?" They will say, "What do you command us?" So he will command them to worship idols, while during that time their provision is abundant and their living is pleasant. Then the Trumpet will be blown, and no one will hear it except that he tilts one side of his neck and raises the other. He said: And the first person to hear it will be a man plastering his camels' watering trough. He said: So he will collapse unconscious, and the people will collapse unconscious. Then Allah will send—or he said: Allah will send down—rain like dew or mist—Nu'man was the one in doubt—from which the bodies of the people will sprout. Then it will be blown again, and behold, they will be standing, looking on. Then it will be said: "O people, come to your Lord! And stop them, for indeed they are to be questioned." He said: Then it will be said: "Bring forth the expedition of the Fire." It will be said: "From how many?" It will be said: "From every 1,000, 999." He said: That is the Day that will turn children grey-haired, and that is the Day when the Shin will be laid bare.'

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and Ibn Numayr narrated to us, both saying: Waki' narrated to us [H]; and Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us: Jarir informed us [H]; and Ibn Abi 'Umar narrated to us: Sufyan narrated to us [H]; and Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us [H]; and Muhammad ibn Rafi' narrated to me: Abu Usamah narrated to us; all of them from Isma'il, with this chain of narration, the like of the hadith of Ibrahim ibn Humayd, and he added in the hadith of Yazid: 'So he said to me: "O my dear son!"'

Surayj ibn Yunus narrated to us: Hushaym narrated to us, from Isma'il, from Qays, from al-Mughirah ibn Shu'bah, who said: No one asked the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) about the Dajjal more than I asked him. He said: 'And what is your question?' He said: I said: 'They say that with him will be mountains of bread and meat, and a river of water.' He said: 'He is more insignificant to Allah than that.'

Shihab ibn 'Abbad al-'Abdi narrated to us: Ibrahim ibn Humayd ar-Ru'asi narrated to us, from Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, from Qays ibn Abi Hazim, from al-Mughirah ibn Shu'bah, who said: No one asked the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) about the Dajjal more than I asked him. He said: 'What troubles you about him? Indeed, he will not harm you.' He said: I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, they say that with him will be food and rivers.' He said: 'He is more insignificant to Allah than that.'

Muhammad ibn 'Abdullah ibn Qahzad, of the people of Marw, narrated to me: 'Abdullah ibn 'Uthman narrated to us, from Abu Hamzah, from Qays ibn Wahb, from Abu al-Waddak, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'The Dajjal will emerge, and a man from among the believers will head towards him. The armed guards—the armed guards of the Dajjal—will meet him and say to him, "Where are you heading?" He will say, "I am heading to this one who has emerged." He said: They will say to him, "Do you not believe in our lord?" He will say, "There is no obscurity concerning our Lord!" So they will say, "Kill him!" But some of them will say to others, "Did your lord not forbid you to kill anyone without him?" He said: So they will take him to the Dajjal. When the believer sees him, he will say, "O people! This is the Dajjal whom the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) mentioned!" He said: The Dajjal will order him to be laid out flat, saying, "Take him and wound his head!" So his back and belly will be thoroughly beaten. He said: Then he will say, "Do you still not believe in me?" He said: So he will say, "You are the lying Messiah!" He said: Then it will be ordered that he be sawn with a saw from the parting of his head until he is split between his legs. He said: Then the Dajjal will walk between the two severed halves, then say to him, "Stand up!" and he will stand upright. He said: Then he will say to him, "Do you believe in me?" He will say, "I have only increased in insight concerning you!" He said: Then he will say, "O people! He will not be able to do this to anyone among mankind after me!" He said: Then the Dajjal will seize him to slaughter him, but the area between his neck to his collarbone will be turned into copper, so he will find no way to kill him. He said: So he will seize him by his hands and feet and cast him away, and the people will think that he cast him into the Fire, but he was only cast into Paradise.' The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'This is the greatest of mankind in martyrdom before the Lord of the worlds.'
And 'Abdullah ibn 'Abd ar-Rahman ad-Darimi narrated to me: Abu al-Yaman informed us: Shu'ayb informed us, from az-Zuhri, in this chain of narration, the like of it.

'Amr an-Naqid, al-Hasan al-Hulwani, and 'Abd ibn Humayd narrated to me—and their wordings are close, and the phrasing is that of 'Abd; he said: 'narrated to me', and the other two said: 'narrated to us'—Ya'qub—and he is Ibn Ibrahim ibn Sa'd—narrated to us: my father narrated to us, from Salih, from Ibn Shihab: 'Ubaydullah ibn 'Abdullah ibn 'Utbah informed me that Abu Sa'id al-Khudri said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) narrated to us one day a long hadith about the Dajjal, and among what he narrated to us was that he said: 'He will come while it is forbidden for him to enter the mountain passes of Medina, so he will halt at one of the salt marshes adjacent to Medina. Then on that day, a man who is the best of people—or among the best of people—will come out to him and say to him, "I testify that you are the Dajjal of whom the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) narrated to us!" So the Dajjal will say, "Do you think that if I kill this man and then bring him back to life, you will have any doubt about the matter?" They will say, "No." He said: So he will kill him, then bring him back to life. Then he will say when he brings him back to life, "By Allah, I was never more certain about you than I am right now!" He said: The Dajjal will want to kill him, but will not be given power over him.' Abu Ishaq said: It is said that this man is al-Khidr (peace be upon him).

'Ali ibn Hujr as-Sa'di narrated to us: 'Abdullah ibn 'Abd ar-Rahman ibn Yazid ibn Jabir and al-Walid ibn Muslim narrated to us—Ibn Hujr said: the narration of one merged into the narration of the other—from 'Abd ar-Rahman ibn Yazid ibn Jabir, with this chain of narration, the like of what we mentioned, and he added after his saying: '"There was once water in this lake." Then they will march on until they reach the Mount of al-Khamar—which is the mountain of Bayt al-Maqdis—and they will say, "We have killed whoever was on earth, come let us kill whoever is in heaven." So they will shoot their arrows into the sky, and Allah will return their arrows to them dyed with blood.' And in the narration of Ibn Hujr: 'For indeed, I have brought forth servants of Mine whom no one has the capacity to fight.'
